chapter: U Street, Jelly Roll Morton, the youth band and the WPA
title: Meeting Jelly Roll Morton, new manager at the Jungle Inn
summary: Miss Lyles introduces him to Jelly Roll Morton, a name that means nothing to him, and Morton plays and name-drops.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: I stayed down there for I guess about three months or so. A short while after that... I don't remember what terminated the job. But a short while after that, I was up on U Street in this particular place where I had worked, the Jungle Inn, where this lady Miss Lyles ran it... I was up there, and everybody was talking about the new manager they have at this club, and they're hinting around that he's Miss Lyles' boyfriend. Some people were saying that he was famous, and other people were making all sorts of comments about him -- and that he played the piano.

So naturally, I went up there, and it was in the day, before the club had started... I went up there actually just to say hello to Miss Lyles and find out what was happening at the same time. And she says, "Oh, John, come on over. I want you to meet Mr. Morton." So I went over and she said, "Mr. Morton. This is the famous Jelly Roll Morton." So I didn't know who Jelly Roll Morton was. The only thing I heard mentioned about Jelly Roll was something Bessie Smith used to sing in a song, and she'd say something about her jelly rolls or something. But I never knew nothing about a man named... I didn't think there was actually a real man named Jelly Roll.
Anyway, I met him, and he talked to me about how long I'd been playing and all that. And he sat down and he played some

things for me, and was talking a lot of things to me that was going in one ear and out the other because it wasn't important to me. I was watching him play the piano, and these names he was calling... I didn't relate to anything! It's so funny how things like that happen. Teaching school now, I have kids that, you mention names like Lester Young or Charlie Parker or somebody to them, and they don't have no idea who you're talking about. And these can be music students. So at that particular time, I had no idea... If he said, for example...mentioned Baby Dodds or somebody, it didn't mean anything to me. But if he said a name like Fletcher Henderson, I would know.
